facebook.caption:
That station is spinning at 68 RPM.

68 RPM sounds harmless until you do the math on a ring that wide: over 150 G's at the outer edge. Cooper and Brand at the hub? Fine. The ship itself? Held together by Hans Zimmer's pipe organ.

Be honest—did the soundtrack distract you from the physics, or did you catch this? 👇

20 world-record deadlifts. Per shoulder. At the same time.

A packed subway train at 70 mph needs ~20 tons of braking force. That's 10 tons on each arm. The webs could actually handle it. Peter's shoulders could not.

Could Tobey's Spider-Man actually survive that pull, or are his arms gone? 👇

Forget Cap's biceps. Look at what he's holding on to.

Be honest—does Cap's bicep give out first, or does that railing rip clean off the roof? 👇

facebook.caption:
Two Chargers vs. a 10-ton vault with no wheels.

Dragging a 10-ton steel vault flat on asphalt takes ~5 tons of pull. A Charger's tires give up under one ton. Real life: a massive burnout and the cops walking up. Movie: Friction: zero. Family: undefeated.

How many Chargers would it actually take to move that vault? Drop your guess 👇

facebook.caption:
Scientists actually ran the numbers on the T. rex chase—and it's not even close.

To run as fast as a car, a 6-ton T. rex would need ~86% of its body to be leg muscle. Newer studies put its top speed around 28 km/h. That Jeep is being chased by a guy on a bicycle.

Did Spielberg get away with this one, or did it ruin the scene for you? 👇

The tank shell isn't what kills him. The landing is.

Does the Mark 3 have secret inertial dampeners, or did Marvel just ignore G-forces here? 👇

facebook.caption:
The fastest breakup anyone has ever survived was Mach 3.

Mach 10 is ~3x faster than a rifle bullet, and wind blast scales with speed squared. The SR-71 pilot who survived Mach 3 in 1966 lost his crewmate. Maverick walks into a diner for water.

Be honest—do you believe the fan theory that Maverick died here and the rest of the movie is a dream? 👇

facebook.caption:
Nolan really flipped a 15-ton semi in Chicago—but he cheated on ONE detail.

They flipped a real semi on a real street with a nitrogen piston, zero CGI. But streetlight bolts are rated for wind, not 15 tons of truck. Gotham apparently bolts its streetlights down tighter than its banks.

Practical stunt is still a 10/10—but did you ever notice the lamppost cables? 👇

facebook.caption:
Bulletproof suits are real. The physics problem isn't the bullet.

Kevlar-lined suits genuinely exist. But stopping a bullet doesn't make it disappear: every hit dents inward like a baseball bat. Fifteen of those and you're not doing judo.

How many hits in a Kevlar suit before you're tapping out? 👇

Hank's own rule: same atoms, same mass.

Tiny Scott still weighs ~200 lb. A flying ant weighs about as much as a grain of rice. That ant isn't lifting 50x its weight. It's lifting about 3 million times its weight.

So is Ant-Man the strongest Avenger, or is it literally just Ant-thony? 👇

facebook.caption:
Could stabbing your own spacesuit actually save you in space?

A spacesuit holds ~4.3 psi, and in a vacuum a leak really does work as a thruster. The problem is steering: thrust from your hand, not your center of mass, means torque. You spin like a deflating balloon.

Would you actually try the "Iron Man" maneuver if you were stranded in orbit? 👇

Wait—if Thor survived a neutron star, how did Thanos knock him out with a punch? 👇

facebook.caption:
355 feet tall, 90,000 tons. An aircraft carrier on two legs.

Scale an animal up and its weight grows faster than its bones (square-cube law). City streets are thin asphalt over tunnels. And his heart has to push blood 15 stories up, over 10x a giraffe's blood pressure.

Forget the military—how many blocks does Godzilla make it before falling into a subway tunnel? 👇
